capabilities: Sync vault files over a persistent WebSocket connection with delta uploads and 3-way merge
Browse sync history and recover previous file versions
Take automatic local snapshots with configurable retention
Publish selected folders as a site with custom domain and appearance options
Share vaults or published sites with other accounts
extras: The server is a separate Python project (pumice-server) you must run yourself; the README warns that syncing plugin code and plugin data.json (both off by default) crosses a larger trust boundary since data.json often holds plaintext API tokens.
intentEvidence: modeled on Obsidian's own built-in Sync plugin, so an edit on one device shows up on another right away
motivation: The README states the goal is to sync instantly no matter how many files are in the vault.
problem: Obsidian's built-in Sync is a hosted paid service, so users who want instant multi-device sync over infrastructure they control have no first-party option.

relations.evidence: modeled on Obsidian's own built-in Sync plugin
syncs your vault with a self-hosted server (pumice-server — required, run it yourself)

requires.name: server account (login via browser token handoff)

summary: Self-hosted sync client that keeps a vault in live sync with your own pumice-server, with history, snapshots, publishing, and vault sharing.
